or outbound.

old:
A secret appears in an artifact only as `vars.secret('ID')` and only as the value argument of
`fill()` — the single approved position in V1. It is rejected in URLs, selectors, key arguments,
assertion arguments and option values. Resolved values are produced by `ValueResolver.secret` at the
moment of the action call, are never placed in operation objects, and every outbound failure message
passes through a redactor that scrubs known values in plain, URL-encoded, double-URL-encoded and
base64 (standard and URL-safe, padded and unpadded) forms.

The redactor scrubs *known* values. It cannot prove an arbitrary string is free of secrets, and
inline credentials that never go through `vars.secret` are invisible here — the backend rejects
known credential patterns before gateway submission (story 10.8).
new:
Current artifact generation is data-only; there is no `vars.secret`, `ValueResolver` or AST
argument execution path. A secret fill carries a value-less `secretRef`/`sourceInputId` tied to
its declared `fill.value` input recipe, step and configuration provenance. Replay receives the
resolved values in its private run metadata, and guided delivery uses its admitted frame. The
observed/guided sections below define the current approved-origin, secret-origin, retained
password-control and names-only authorization boundaries; none permits secret values in URLs,
selectors, assertions or other argument slots. Outbound diagnostics and failure messages redact
known values, including their supported encoded variants, before bounds or writes.

The redactor scrubs *known* values. It cannot prove an arbitrary string is free of secrets or
make inline credentials safe. The backend's pre-gateway credential checks and current
observed/guided secret-use policy remain required.
